Introduction

Revision Questions

Bayesian Models allow for the dealing of uncertain or probabilistic data within AI. They are part of a larger subset of models known as graphical models. Bayesian models are very different to the previously explored neural networks.

Black Box Models

Problems with Lack of Explainability

  • The responses of individual neurons within this type of model are not known and are considered too complex for a human to understand figuratively.
  • In a black box model, the internal behaviour of the code is not known or understood very well. We may know that it uses convolutions but the inner workings are difficult to comprehend.

The underlying mechanisms of the black box must be opened in order to gain the trust of users and make better decisions.

XAI: Explainable AI

Explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) is a set of processes and methods that allows human users to comprehend and trust the results and output created by machine learning algorithms.

Counterfactuals
If X had not occurred, Y would have not occurred

Probability Overview

  • Probability allows us to assign a number between 0 and 1 to an event
    e.g. tossing a coin as 0.5
  • Something with a probability of 1 is necessarily true meaning it will definitely happen, whereas a probability of 0 will be necessarily false

Conditional Probability (basic stuff)

  • Refers to probabilities that are based on previous circumstances.
  • E.g. probability of a headache given that you have flu

    (probability of headache AND flu are not independent)

  • Probability of B given A...
    is the probability of A and B...
    divided by the probability of A

Example
Headache and Flu not independent
P(H) = 1/10
P(F) = 1/40
P(H|F) = 1/2

Therefore, we can say it is at least 50% likely that someone with flu will have a headache.

  • Keep in mind that probabilities are directional...
  • $P(F|H) is not the same as P(H|F)

Bayes Theorem

  • Allows us to flip the conditional.
  • Probability that I have a headache, given I have flu...
    • equals the probability of flu given I have a headache...
    • …times the probability of having a headache...
    • …all divided by the probability that I have flu

Bayes Theorem is extremely important within AI for calculating new conditional probabilities from old ones.

Probability Distributions

  • A distribution of a range of possible scenarios must add up to 1.
  • All possible event outcomes are assigned a probability.

Joint Probability

  • How do we calculate the probability of all possible outcomes for lots of different non-independent columns/variables?
    Written as )

A joint probability distribution can answer this question.

Joint Distribution Example

What is the probability of a toothache, given you have a cavity? 0.04

Causality

  • Causality refers to how events 'cause'/influence other events
  • It is key to understanding, reasoning and explanations.
  • Graph-based approaches can model causal relationships
  • This allows for human-like inferences similar to those shown in expert systems, as opposed to the deep learning inferences.

Causal Network Example

  • Nodes map directly to features in your dataset
  • This graph is the 'hello world' of Bayesian networks
  • The alarm can be set off by both a burglary or an earthquake

Reasoning Examples

  • Which parts are independent of others?
    • If the alarm is sounding it makes no difference whether its a burglary or an earthquake
    • Explaining Away Effect: Multiple causes for one situation.
    • Burglary and Earthquake are independent...
      • but if you know the alarm is sounding, they become dependent
      • If the alarm is sounding, and we know its an earthquake, the probability of a burglary goes down as it's been 'explained away'
